title: normalize-openai-tool-priority-mapping-and-stable-stream-framing
author: Aisha Kaur
description:
Motivation: Users integrating OpenAI-style function/tool calling have reported two recurring issues: 1) inconsistent selection semantics when multiple compatible tools exist (racey tool_choice scoring), and 2) truncated or mis-ordered tool messages during streaming handoffs. This PR introduces a compact, explicit mapping layer between OpenAI tool descriptors and Redwood's internal tool adapters, plus a stream-framing locator that guarantees atomic tool message boundaries across chunked SSE/WebSocket streams.

Summary of changes: normalize incoming tool schema fields (type hints, enums, required/optional semantics), add a deterministic priority resolution for OpenAI 'tool_choice' scenarios, emit lightweight selection provenance metadata for downstream observability, and implement a stream-framed locator token inserted into streaming frames to demarcate tool invocation payloads so consumers can reassemble tool input reliably.

Design highlights: - Tool mapping: a new mapping table (openai_to_adapter) flattens OpenAI-style parameter schemas into Redwood-compatible parameter templates. The mapper supports: aliasing, type coercions (string->int/float), default injection, parameter renaming (snake_case). This keeps the public API stable while allowing internal adapter evolution. - Priority semantics: when the model supplies multiple tool_choice candidates, we apply an ordered, deterministic comparator that factors: explicit model-provided score, schema specificity (number of required params matched), adapter capability flags (sync/async), and configured customer preferred_tiers. This comparator is deterministic across nodes to avoid split-brain tool races. - Streaming framing: all tool-bound streaming fragments include a minimal locator header: "rw-tl:ID:seq:flags" where ID is a request-scoped UUID, seq is a monotonic fragment index, and flags signals final/partial frames and schema version. Consumers must buffer frames with the same ID and assemble in seq order; the runtime enforces monotonicity and will close the stream on out-of-order delivery. - Backwards compatibility: Incoming simple tool call payloads without explicit tool_choice still work. The mapper defaults to best-effort matching. We add a compatibility flag (OPENAI_TOOL_MAP=v1) for gradual rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Mapping logic implemented in api/compat/openai_tool_mapper.go - [x] Stable stream framing implemented in runtime/stream/framer.go - [x] Unit tests for priority comparator and mapping rules - [x] Integration test with streaming simulator and ts-sdk mock - [x] Documentation update in docs/openai-compat.md (compat section) - [x] Feature gated behind OPENAI_TOOL_MAP env var

Rollout plan: feature is off by default. Start dark rollout for 1% of hosted requests in us-west-2 for 48h, monitor tool-invoke mismatch metric and stream-reassembly-failures. If stable, ramp to 25% then 100% over 7 days. For Dedicated customers, enable by request with opt-in toggles in the console.

Related work and references: Linear ENG-1245 tracks multi-tool priority regressions; ENG-1302 is the streaming stability spike. See docs/internal/stream-framing.md for the framing contract.

Notes: kept the mapping table intentionally small and expressible so we can ship without a schema migration. The streaming locator is designed to add <1% overhead to token payload size.

release_notes: Enhancement: OpenAI compatibility - deterministic tool selection and stable stream framing for tool/function calls. Feature gated behind OPENAI_TOOL_MAP. Improves reliability of tool invocations over streaming transports.
